sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
பாதி உடல் பாவைக்குப் பகிர்ந்தளித்த பரமனே
வேதி இடை அவிர்பாகம் ஏற்கும் வேணியனே
sections.translit:
pAdhi udal pAvaikkup pagirndhaLittha paramanE
vEdhi idai avirbhAgam ERkum vENiyanE
sections.en: Oh Supreme Lord, you shared half of your body with your consort. Oh Lord Siva with matted locks, you heartily accept your share of the offering during a yagna inside the Vedic pit, or sacrificial fireplace.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
ஓதி நின்ற மறையரெலாம் உன்னிசை பாட
நீதி இதுவேயென்று ஆதிசக்தியை அணைத்தே
sections.translit:
Odhi nindRa maRaiyarelAm unnisai pAda
nIdhi idhuvEyendRu Adhisakthiyai aNaitthE
sections.en: All Vedic scholars who chant scriptures sing your glory. You stated that this is real justice and embraced your consort, offering her half of your body.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
சோதியே ஓளிவெள்ளமாய் இருளகற்றும் ஈசனே
நாதியே இல்லாது உன் நாமம் ஓதி நின்றேன்
பீதியே குடிகொண்ட என்னுளம் உறைய வேண்டும்
ஆதியே இலா சிவனேயுன் மலர்ப்பாதம் அருள வேண்டும்
sections.translit:
sOdhiyE oLiveLLamAy iruLagatRum IsanE
nAdhiyE illAdhu un nAmam Odhi nindREn
bIdhiyE kudikoNda ennuLam uRaiya vENdum
AdhiyE ilA sivanEyun malarppAdham aruLa vENdum
sections.en: You are the dazzling light. Ever present as a flood of brilliance you are the Lord that removes darkness. I stood chanting your name with no support around me. Please dwell in my fear-dominated heart. Oh, Lord Shiva you are eternal and have no beginning.  Please offer your lotus feet and bless me.

notes: The first line of the Pallavi and the second line of Anupallavi refer to Siva offering half of his body to Goddess Parvathi and becoming Ardhanaareeswara. This is supposed to have occurred in the sacred shrine of Thiruvannamalai. Recall that this is also the shrine where Siva presented as a column of fire and hence the use of the word (sOdhiyE) to address him in the charanam. For details, see the sthalapuranam of the Arunachaleshwara temple in Thiruvannamalai. Siva offered half body to Parvathi There are other mythologies associated with this shrine. No one including celestials could stand the heat when Siva stood as a column of fire. Lord Siva transformed himself into a mountain and was called Arunachalam. The day Siva offered one half of his body to Goddess Parvathi has become a festive Karthigai day now. For more rare information regarding Thiruvannamalai, see: அறிந்த ஆலயங்கள் அபூர்வ தகவல்கள், விகடன் பிரசுரம், 757 அண்ணா சாலை, சென்னை 600002, விற்பனை பிரிவு போன்: 091-44-42634283/ 84, முதற் பதிப்பு: பிப்ரவரி 2008, பக்கம் 38 – 49. The divine word “வேணியன் (vEnian)”appears in Sekkizhar’s Periya puranam in the introductory verse. Siva who has the matted locks, is addressed as vENiyan by Sekkizhar.
